trial.title: Real Chess Training — Trial
trial.goal: The Goal: Train your decision-making under pressure.

process.title: The Process
process.timer: Start the clock and begin with the first diagram.
process.manage: Some problems require deep calculation; others demand quicker practical choices.
process.commit: Write down only one solution per puzzle, exactly as you would execute it in a real game scenario.
process.stop: When the timer rings, write down your final decision for your current position and immediately stop.
process.review: Take a physical break, then watch the breakdown video to audit your thought process and learn from each position.

mindset.title: The Mindset
mindset.struggle: These tests are deliberately difficult; you might score 0 points now and then, that’s okay.
mindset.wall: When you hit the „I can’t solve this“ moment, force yourself to commit to the least bad option you can find.
mindset.process: Stop judging the final outcome, and start analyzing how you make decisions when you feel stuck.
mindset.goodEnough: This training mimics real game play. You don’t need to find the top engine move all the time, what matters is finding a decent move.

trial.golden: Write down exactly one choice per position, every single time. We are training the habit of making a definitive decision under pressure, regardless of your confidence level.

benefits.title: Your Benefits
benefits.confidence: Increased confidence in doing hard things
benefits.keyMoments: Distinguish between key moments and „good enough“ positions
benefits.easier: Games will feel easier — your training was harder than a real game!

review.title: Review
review.later: Work through all six positions first — then audit your thinking with the breakdown video.
review.ready: All positions committed — time for the breakdown video.

timeLimit.title: 45 minutes are up
timeLimit.body: Per the guidelines: write down your final decision for your current position — and stop. The test is deliberately hard; an honest hard stop is part of the training.
timeLimit.review: Then take a physical break and watch the breakdown video on the trial page to audit your thought process.
